direction.comments: The direction on a macro scale is great, as it creates a very tense and suspenseful atmosphere that feels unique and fresh for the 'possession' subgenre, creating a world that makes the viewer want to have one eye closed and the other peeking to see what happens next; The direction on a micro scale is good for the most part, as you learn a lot about these characters since their relationships are what make this movie so terrifying, though it does suffer from generic horror acting sequences at times; The storytelling is very good, as it slowly unravels the theme of 'being careful what you wish for' because by the end of the movie, it becomes total chaos, planting roots throughout to make the ending feel well-deserved; The filmmakers build tension masterfully, as the whole movie is a tense and suspenseful environment that makes you want to crawl into your seat; I really respect that this movie did not rely on jump scares and instead focused on psychological horror, which prevented it from feeling like a cheap horror movie because it works for its scares, having a high follow-through rate

performance.comments: Plays his role well as he embodies the socially anxious/lonely generation of young male adults who are afraid to express their feelings and do the right thing, as he knows what he is doing is wrong but is too afraid to change it; he really embodies the male loneliness epidemic well as your perception of him throughout the movie turns from being relatable to being despised the way he handles the situation he's got himself in

A true star in the making as she plays both the original Nikki and the 'obsessed' version of Nikki very well as you can feel the dichotomy between the two characters; the original Nikki really does feel like a friend, while the 'obsessed' version is terrifying to watch on screen because of the lengths she will go to show Bear she loves him more than 'anyone in the entire world'; the switches between the personas also feel very fluid and helps show what is real and what is fake; has very good chemistry with Michael Johnston as their interactions are both heartwarming and terrifying, creating a sense of unease that slowly builds throughout the movie; she really is a scene stealer as her presence fills the entire room, making her so captivating to watch
Plays the comedic relief side character well

Acts as the voice of reason for the group as it feels like she is the only character with ambition and common sense, wanting what's best for Bear; because of this, she has a good dynamic with Bear as their chemistry is second best to Nikki and Bear
Funny he's in this movie, but he is basically you typical 'bigger' actor to help get this movie funding since he doesn't really have that much of a role

cast.comments: There isn't too much of a supporting cast, but the cast feels close-knit to show the friend group dynamic well, especially for young adults who work together

story.comments: The concept is very good and unique, a fresh take on the 'possession' subgenre as it explores the lengths Bear will go to have his crush fall in love with him, forcing him to be 'careful what he wished for'; The plot structure is linear and standard; Character writing is very good, as the movie is a character study of Bear, a young adult who resembles the current generation by facing social anxiety and fearing the expression of feelings, showing the lengths he must go to hide how he feels and avoid doing the right thing; The character writing for Nikki is also good, as the dichotomy between her character before and after the 'obsession' takes over is very well done, illustrating what is real and what is forced; On a second watch, the movie really does play like a character study of the four main characters: the tortured one, the immoral one, the jealous one, and the righteous one

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is very sharp for a low-budget horror movie, as it feels realistic for these young adult characters and adds a sense of unease during the horror sequences; The dialogue is also very intentional, as even the smallest of phrases has the biggest meaning in terms of what is reality and what Bear wants to be reality; The humor is surprisingly good and helps alleviate the tension to make the horror sequences enjoyable to an extent, showcasing the comedic background of the director; The symbolism is pretty surface-level, as the movie's messaging is mostly about being 'careful what you wish for' and presenting a character study of a young adult who is afraid of sharing how he feels and doing the right thing; The foreshadowing is very good in this movie, as it sets up the ending very well and makes the movie feel bookended; On a second watch, you really do see how masterful the foreshadowing is, as they plant roots and subtle hints throughout the movie that help you see through the fog of this wishful world and help make the ending justified

score.comments: The score does a good job of building the tone and atmosphere of the movie, as it makes the horror sequences feel like they are crescendoing into something that is very hard to watch while you visibly feel unease with what is occurring on-screen

soundtrack.comments: The soundtrack helps build the world for this young adult friend group, as it uses a lot of indie and alternative music

cinematography.comments: The cinematography is well-executed for a low-budget horror film and makes this movie look unique; The cinematography is integral to building the suspense and tension of the horror sequences, as the constant slow zoom-ins and quick pans are vital in creating a sense of unease; The use of lighting between Bear and Nikki also really amplifies the characters, as having Nikki always show up in a dark setting makes her feel like a 'sleep paralysis demon' who makes Bear constantly question if this is real; I really enjoyed the 1.50:1 aspect ratio, as it created a sense of claustrophobia and made the movie look unique

editing.comments: The editing is instrumental in building the suspense and tension, as it uses a lot of slow zooms and quick cuts to create an uneasy feeling; Also, for a low-budget horror movie, the editing feels very innovative and unique, as it makes this movie look like it is in a league of its own

sound.comments: The sound is crisp and does an amazing job of building tension and suspense throughout the movie, making you want to crawl into your seat

visual_effects.comments: The use of practical effects really built the gore of the horror sequences, as it adds another level of suspense that makes this movie hard to watch in a good way; The money-falling sequence looked quite fake, though

review.pacing: The pacing is good, as it constantly shifts from slow to fast to create a rush of suspense that builds up the horror sequences; The runtime is a bit long, but cutting five to ten minutes really would not change much
review.climax: The climax is executed very well, as it helps the movie stick the landing and feel like a complete story, which is something modern horror movies struggle with
review.tone: The tone is very much that of a psychological horror movie, though the way it mixes in comedy makes the movie feel like a fresh take on the genre
review.overall: Overall, 'Obsession' is a great horror movie elevated by its meticulous writing, well-executed direction and horror sequences, and a tour de force performance from Inde Navarrette, all of which make this movie feel like a fresh take on the possession subgenre and a modern horror classic, sticking the landing in a way that very few modern horror movies do
